records.text: The Spaniard who traveled widely throughout the southeastern region of North America from 1539 to 1542 was Spanish conquistador Hernando de Soto.

Hernando de Soto led an expedition through the region that is now the southeastern United States from 1539 to 1542. The expedition traveled through present-day Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina, Tennessee, Alabama, Mississippi, Arkansas, and Oklahoma, among other places.

Hernando de Soto’s expedition encountered many Native American tribes. The expedition contributed to the spread of diseases including smallpox and influenza, which had a significant impact on Indigenous populations.
